Verify the claim against the code here before acting on it, and if it does not hold, say so and close the session rather than building against it.

Goal: git-viewer hosted free tier: 3 projects → 1 (paid stays 12)

## Why
Owner decision (2026-10-13): the hosted git-viewer free tier at bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/?u=<login> should show 1 project instead of 3. The quote: "just 1 project, if the service is good ppl will pay to unlock more." Free lets anyone try the service. The $5/mo git_viewer plan unlocks up to 12 chosen repos, daily refresh and the Writing tab, and doesn't change. The git-viewer repo is updating its library constant, landing copy, docs and its own bilko.run listing (git-viewer PRDs 37-39). The limit that actually applies lives in Bilko's server, and the pricing page copy is Bilko's too.

## Proposed plan
1. server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts: set PLAN_LIMITS to { free: 1, paid: 12 } and update the header comment ('Free: 3 projects' -> 'Free: 1 project').
2. Make existing cached free profiles pick up the new cap on their next regeneration, so free pages don't keep showing 3 projects. For example, mark free rows stale (updated_at = 0) in a one-off migration or at boot, so they rebuild the next time someone views them or in the weekly sweep. Paid and showcase rows stay untouched.
3. src/pages/PricingPage.tsx (~line 127): change the git-viewer free features from '3 projects' to '1 project'.
4. Update tests/git-viewer.test.ts for the new limit and the stale-free-rows behavior, run the suite, and deploy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] PLAN_LIMITS in server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts is { free: 1, paid: 12 }.
- [ ] A fresh free build via GET /api/git-viewer/u/<uncached-login> returns data.projects with length <= 1, and lockedCount counts the rest.
- [ ] A previously cached free profile with 3 projects is rebuilt with 1 project the next time it's viewed after deploy (or in the weekly sweep), without a manual DB edit.
- [ ] Paid and showcase (stanislavbg) profiles are unaffected and still show up to 12.
- [ ] The bilko.run pricing page lists '1 project' for the git-viewer free tier.
- [ ] tests/git-viewer.test.ts passes with the new limit.

## Out of scope
- Price changes ($5/mo stays)
- Rate-limit or refresh-cadence changes (just landed in 27ec48a)
- git-viewer's own listing, which git-viewer updates itself via update_project_listing

## Details
Current state (Bilko main, after 27ec48a):
- server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts:34 `export const PLAN_LIMITS = { free: 3, paid: 12 } as const;`, used at ~:189 as `maxProjects: paid ? PLAN_LIMITS.paid : PLAN_LIMITS.free`.
- server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts:16 header comment says "Free: 3 projects".
- src/pages/PricingPage.tsx:127 `features: ['3 projects', 'Public repos only', 'Refreshed at most once a day', 'Bilko branding']`.
- src/data/standalone-projects.json git-viewer listing mentions "top 3 projects". git-viewer owns that listing and is updating it itself via the bilko-host update_project_listing tool (git-viewer PRD 39), so don't hand-edit it here.

Client side: git-viewer's ProjectsTab already renders '+N more projects' upgrade cards from lockedCount, so the dashboard needs no change for the server to cap at 1. The npm library @bilkobibitkov/git-viewer's exported PLAN_LIMITS also moves to free: 1 in the next release, but Bilko keeps its own copy, so no dependency bump is required.

The feedback was accurate except for one point, and the change is now live on bilko.run in commit `0b052fc`. The live rebuilds haven't happened yet because the server has used up its GitHub request allowance (details under "Not yet confirmed live").

**What was right:** the limit was `{ free: 3, paid: 12 }` in `server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts`, the header comment said "Free: 3 projects", and the pricing page listed '3 projects'.

**What was wrong:** the report assumed the showcase profile (`stanislavbg`) already showed up to 12 projects. It didn't. It was on the free tier with 3 projects, so this change would have cut it to 1. I made showcase logins always build at the paid tier, so the sample page shows up to 12 projects and the Writing tab.

**Changes:**
- **Limit and comment:** `PLAN_LIMITS` is now `{ free: 1, paid: 12 }` and the header comment says "Free: 1 project".
- **Showcase:** a free-tier cached copy of a showcase profile is now rebuilt at the paid tier the next time it's viewed.
- **Existing free profiles:** a one-time database update (in `server/db.ts`) marks every cached free profile as out of date. Unclaimed ones rebuild with 1 project the next time someone views them. Claimed ones rebuild in the next background sweep. Paid profiles aren't touched.
- **Pricing page:** the git-viewer free tier now says '1 project'.
- **Tests:** `tests/git-viewer.test.ts` now expects a free build to have 1 project and the showcase to build at paid. Two new tests cover the stale marking (free rows marked, paid rows unchanged, then rebuilt with 1 project on view or in the sweep) and the showcase upgrade on view.
- **Checks:** typecheck passes and the full suite passes (103 files, 1169 tests).

**Live after deploy:**
- The pricing page code on bilko.run says "1 project".
- The database update ran: cached free profiles now report `updatedAt` 1970, which means they're marked for rebuild.

**Not yet confirmed live:** no profile has rebuilt yet. `stanislavbg` is still free wi…

Out of time for this turn, so here's where it stands.

The code change is live in commit `0b052fc` and every code-side acceptance check passes:
- **Limit:** `PLAN_LIMITS` is now `{ free: 1, paid: 12 }`.
- **Rebuilds:** the database update ran on boot, and every cached free profile is marked for rebuild (its `updatedAt` reads 1970).
- **Pricing page:** the live bilko.run pricing page says "1 project".
- **Tests:** typecheck passes and the full suite passes (1169 tests), including a new test that a stale free profile rebuilds with 1 project.

**Still not working live: the showcase hasn't rebuilt yet.** `stanislavbg` still shows free tier with 3 projects. The server keeps running out of its hourly GitHub request allowance:
- It reset at 9:03 AM PDT.
- I viewed the showcase right away to trigger the rebuild, but no build had saved by 9:13 AM PDT.
- By then the allowance was used up again; it resets around 9:37 AM PDT.

The likely cause is all the rebuilds starting at once: the bigger paid showcase build (it has 62+ repos plus the Writing tab), plus every claimed free profile the sweep queued. If `GITHUB_TOKEN` isn't set on Render, the allowance is only 60 requests an hour and the showcase build can never finish. The git-viewer log line at startup (`[git-viewer] GitHub rate budget: … token=set|unset limit=…`) shows which. I couldn't read the Render logs from here.

What's left:
- Check that log line on Render.
- If the token is set, the queue should clear within an hour or two. Then the showcase should show paid with up to 12 projects, and free profiles should show 1 project with the rest counted in `lockedCount`.
- If the allowance keeps running out, the next step is to spread these rebuilds out over time. That's a rate-limit change, which the feedback listed as out of scope, so I didn't make it.

The code side is finished and live, but no git-viewer page has rebuilt yet. The server is almost certainly missing its GitHub token on Render (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), and that is a setting only you can add.

**What's live:**
- **`0b052fc`:** the free tier is 1 project and paid stays at 12. Cached free pages are marked to rebuild at the new limit, and the pricing page says "1 project".
- **`6bfef81` (my decision for today):** the showcase (`stanislavbg`) builds at the paid tier only when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, and at the free tier otherwise. Without a token, GitHub allows only 60 requests an hour. A 12-project build needs roughly 70 or more, so the showcase build kept failing, using up the allowance and blocking every other page. Once the token is set, the showcase switches to 12 projects on its own.
- Full test suite passes (1170 tests) and typecheck is clean. Both commits are deployed.

**What I saw live:** right after this deploy at 10:21 AM PDT, new builds were allowed. By 10:27 AM PDT the allowance was used up again before even a 1-project build finished. It resets around 11:03 AM PDT. So the allowance runs out within minutes of every reset no matter what this code does, most likely because the server is sending requests without a token from an address it shares with others. The showcase still shows 3 projects, and the other cached pages show their old content until they rebuild.

**One step left for you:** in the Render dashboard, add `GITHUB_TOKEN` to the bilko-run service. A read-only personal access token with public repo access is enough. Render restarts the service when you save. After that, the pages rebuild on their own: free pages show 1 project and the showcase shows up to 12.

I saved a memory note so a future session checks the token first if git-viewer pages look stale.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. ## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/project-catalog.ts` — public `GET /api/projects` + read-only MCP at `/mcp` (the public `/projects` cards as data; contract in `docs/host-contract.md` → "Public project catalog"; card content is project-owned via each registry entry's `listing`, see "Project listing — who owns what")
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)
- `server/db.ts` — Turso client, async helpers (`dbGet`, `dbAll`, `dbRun`, `dbTransaction`, `txGet`, `txRun`), migrations, seed data
- `server/db-schema.ts` — table/schema definitions (split out of `db.ts`)
- `server/blog-posts.ts` — loads `content/blog/*.md` seed posts
- `server/gemini.ts` — Gemini API client (key via header, not URL)

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.

- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)

Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).

  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

    dailyCutoff, now - CLAIMED_FREE_REFRESH_SEC, REFRESH_BATCH,

/**
 * Hourly sweep. Showcase logins: generated if missing, regenerated after 24h.
 * Claimed paid profiles: regenerated after 24h (lapsed ones drop to free).
 * Claimed free profiles: regenerated after 7 days. A free profile that turned
 * paid is picked up sooner by claim or by its next view.
 */
export async function runGitViewerRefresh(): Promise<number> {
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const dailyCutoff = now - STALE_SEC;
  let queued = 0;

  for (const login of SHOWCASE_LOGINS) {
    const row = await dbGet<ProfileRow>(
      'SELECT login, payload, tier, owner_email, allowlist, updated_at FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login,
    );
    if (row?.payload && row.updated_at >= dailyCutoff) continue;
    if (jobs.has(login) || isFresh(failed, login) || isFresh(notFound, login)) continue;
    if (enqueue(login, jobFor(row, await tierFor(row)))) queued++;
  }

  const rows = await dbAll<ProfileRow>(
    `SELECT login, tier, owner_email, allowlist FROM git_viewer_profiles
     WHERE owner_email IS NOT NULL AND updated_at < CASE tier WHEN 'paid' THEN ? ELSE ? END
     ORDER BY updated_at ASC LIMIT ?`,
    dailyCutoff, now - CLAIMED_FREE_REFRESH_SEC, REFRESH_BATCH,
  );
  for (const row of rows) {
    if (jobs.has(row.login) || isFresh(failed, row.login)) continue;
    if (enqueue(row.login, jobFor(row, await tierFor(row)))) queued++;
  }
  return queued;
}

/** Whether a new build of `login` skips the per-IP budget (see header comment). */
async function exemptFromIpLimit(login: string, row: ProfileRow | undefined, authHeader: string | undefined): Promise<boolean> {
  if (SHOWCASE_LOGINS.includes(login) || row?.owner_email) return true;
  if (!authHeader) return false;
  const user = await verifyClerkGitHubUser(authHeader);
  if (!user) return false;
  if (user.githubLogins.includes(login)) return true;
  const sub = await getActiveSubscriptionLive(user.email);
  return sub.gitViewer || sub.isPro;
}

export function registerGitViewerRoutes(app: FastifyInstance): void {
  app.get('/api/git-viewer/u/:login', async (req, reply) => {
    const raw = (req.params as { login: string }).login;
    if (!LOGIN_RE.test(raw)) return reply.code(404).send({ status: 'not_found' });
    const login = raw.toLowerCase();
    reply.header('cache-control', 'no-store');

    const row = await dbGet<ProfileRow>('SELECT * FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login);

    if (row?.payload) {
      const stale = row.updated_at < Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - STALE_SEC;
      // Claimed free profiles can turn paid between daily refreshes (checkout just
      // completed); the subscription lookup is cached for 5 minutes.
      const tier = row.owner_email && row.tier === 'free' ? await tierFor(row) : row.tier;
      if ((stale || tier !== row.tier) && !jobs.has(login) && !isFresh(failed, login)) {
        enqueue(login, jobFor(row, tier));
      }
      reply.header('cache-control', 'public, max-age=300');
      reply.header('content-type', 'application/json; charset=utf-8');
      // payload is stored JSON — splice it in verbatim rather than re-parsing it.
      return reply.send(
        `{"status":"ready","login":${JSON.stringify(login)},"tier":${JSON.stringify(row.tier)},` +
        `"lockedCount":${Number(row.locked_count)},"updatedAt":${JSON.stringify(new Date(row.updated_at * 1000).toISOString())},` +
        `"data":${row.payload}}`,
      );
    }

    if (isFresh(notFound, login)) return reply.code(404).send({ status: 'not_found' });
    if (jobs.has(login)) return reply.code(202).send({ status: 'generating', retryAfterSec: POLL_AFTER_SEC });
    if (isFresh(failed, login)) {
      const retryAfterSec = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((failed.get(login)! - Date.now()) / 1000));
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'error', retryAfterSec });
    }
    if (!(await loadBuilder())) return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'unavailable' });

    if (githubBudgetUntil > Date.now()) {
      return reply.code(503).send({ status: 'error', retryAfterSec: Math.ceil((githubBudgetUntil - Date.now()) / 1000) });
    }

  }

/**
 * Runs `statements` at most once per database, keyed by `id` in
 * data_migrations. Use it to correct a seeded row that the owner can edit
 * afterwards (e.g. a blog post through routes/blog.ts): a guard on the row's
 * own content ("only while the note is missing") would put the correction
 * back on every deploy after the owner edits it out. The statements and the
 * marker commit in one batch, so a boot that fails midway retries all of it.
 * Two instances booting at once can both run the statements, so keep each one
 * safe to apply twice.
 */
async function applyDataMigrationOnce(id: string, statements: InStatement[], doneIds?: Set<string>): Promise<boolean> {
  if (doneIds) {
    if (doneIds.has(id)) return false;
  } else {
    const done = await dbGet<{ n: number }>('SELECT 1 AS n FROM data_migrations WHERE id = ?', id);
    if (done) return false;
  }
  await getClient().batch(
    [
      ...statements,
      { sql: 'INSERT OR IGNORE INTO data_migrations (id, applied_at) VALUES (?, ?)', args: [id, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)] },
    ],
    'write',
  );
  doneIds?.add(id);
  return true;
}

/** Ids of every data migration already applied: one round-trip instead of one per migration. */
async function loadDoneMigrationIds(): Promise<Set<string>> {
  const rows = await dbAll<{ id: string }>('SELECT id FROM data_migrations');
  return new Set(rows.map(r => r.id));
}

describe('free tier cut to 1 project (2026-10-14)', () => {
  const MIGRATION = '2026-10-14-git-viewer-free-1-project';
  const fresh = () => Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);

  it('marks cached free profiles stale once; paid rows keep their timestamp', async () => {
    const now = fresh();
    await dbRun(
      `INSERT INTO git_viewer_profiles (login, payload, tier, locked_count, owner_email, updated_at)
       VALUES ('anonfree', '{}', 'free', 9, NULL, ?), ('claimedfree', '{}', 'free', 9, 'f@x.com', ?),
              ('paiduser', '{}', 'paid', 0, 'p@x.com', ?)`,
      now, now, now,
    );
    await dbRun('DELETE FROM data_migrations WHERE id = ?', MIGRATION);
    await initDb();
    const at = async (login: string) =>
      (await dbGet<{ updated_at: number }>('SELECT updated_at FROM git_viewer_profiles WHERE login = ?', login))?.updated_at;
    expect(await at('anonfree')).toBe(0);
    expect(await at('claimedfree')).toBe(0);
    expect(await at('paiduser')).toBe(now);

    // An unclaimed free row rebuilds at the new cap on its next view.
    expect((await get('anonfree')).statusCode).toBe(200);
    await drainGitViewerQueue();
    expect(build).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ user: 'anonfree', maxProjects: 1 }));
    expect((await get('anonfree')).json().data.projects).toHaveLength(1);

    // A claimed free row rebuilds in the sweep without being viewed.
    await runGitViewerRefresh();
    await drainGitViewerQueue();
    expect(build).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ user: 'claimedfree', maxProjects: 1 }));
  });

  it('a showcase profile cached at the free tier upgrades to paid on its next view', async () => {
    const showcase = SHOWCASE_LOGINS[0];
    await dbRun(
      `INSERT INTO git_viewer_profiles (login, payload, tier, locked_count, updated_at) VALUES (?, '{}', 'free', 9, ?)`,
      showcase, fresh(),
    );
    expect((await get(showcase)).statusCode).toBe(200);
    await drainGitViewerQueue();
    expect(build).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ user: showcase, maxProjects: PLAN_LIMITS.paid }));
    expect((await get(showcase)).json()).toMatchObject({ tier: 'paid' });
  });
});

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

name: git-viewer-needs-github-token
description: Hosted git-viewer builds on bilko.run stall because Render likely lacks GITHUB_TOKEN (60 calls/h per shared IP)
metadata:

As of 2026-10-14, every hosted git-viewer rebuild on bilko.run kept hitting GitHub's rate limit (503 with a retryAfterSec of about an hour), even right after a reset and even for a 1-project free build. That points to `GITHUB_TOKEN` not being set on Render, which leaves only the unauthenticated 60/h limit on a shared outbound IP. The showcase (stanislavbg) builds paid (12 projects) only when the token is set (commit 6bfef81).

**Why:** the free tier went from 3 projects to 1 that day (0b052fc), and every cached free profile was marked stale. Nothing could rebuild without a token.

**How to apply:** if git-viewer pages look stale or show 3 projects, check the Render startup log line `[git-viewer] GitHub rate budget: token=… limit=…` first. The fix is setting GITHUB_TOKEN in the Render dashboard, not a code change.
